newsitem.title: USA: Carlisle to acquire Johnson Controls plastics unit.
newsitem.headline: Carlisle to acquire Johnson Controls plastics unit.

text.p: Carlisle Cos. Inc., a manufacturer of automotive and industrial products, said Monday it is in advanced negotiations to acquire the Engineered Plastics Division of Milwaukee-based Johnson Controls Inc.
Terms of the transaction, which Carlisle said it expects to close in the next few weeks, were not disclosed.
Johnson's Engineered Plastics Division, with annualized sales of about $130 million, has two manufacturing facilities in Erie, Pa., one in Lapeer, Mich. and one in Tuscaloosa, Ala.
The unit produces precision-moulded engine components and blow-moulded bumper beams that are supplied to most major automakers in North America.

"The acquisition of EPD (Engineered Plastics Division) enhances and extends Carlisle's component supplier strategy, which involves providing full design, engineering and production services to Tier I companies supplying complete systems to the automotive OEMs (original equipment manufacturers)," said Stephen Munn, chief executive officer of Carlisle.

"EPD adds additional design, process and technical expertise to produce technologically advanced components, including the use of highly engineered resins required for heat resistant applications," Munn added.
The unit will be combined with Carlisle's Geauga unit, also a supplier of components to the automotive industry.
Carlisle's stock was up 25 cents to $53.125 in morning trade on the New York Stock Exchange. Johnson Controls gained 12.5 cents to $75.625, also on the NYSE.
